findings.description: The reroute to T-005 fixed the checker family but not the evidence route, so the same defect survives in a fourth coat: the check names output that bats does not emit, and the fallback it degrades to cannot detect the clause's own named defect. T-005's check_method says 'read the output of the four <script>: all items succeed prints no failure summary cases and FAIL on any failure summary, bare heading, zero-count, or stray blank line from an empty array expansion.' All four cases capture the script through bats `run`, which puts stdout and stderr into $output rather than emitting them, and a passing case emits nothing. I ran `bats --show-output-of-passing-tests --filter 'all items succeed' tests/install-failures.bats` and got four bare `ok` lines and no script output at all. There is therefore no bats invocation that produces the evidence the check_method tells the checker to read. A checker following the instruction literally has two options and the check_method names neither: reconstruct each of the four runs by hand (render the template under the real $HOME, rebuild that case's stubs, execute under a synthetic $HOME, capture the output), or read the four `ok` lines and conclude the clause is satisfied. The second is the default path, and it substitutes the artifact's own assertions for the clause's rubric, which is exactly the self-report the checker contract forbids. Those assertions are strictly narrower than the rubric. I proved the gap rather than argued it: injecting `echo "Failed extensions: ${#failed[@]}"` into the success branch of run_onchange_install-vscode-extensions.sh.tmpl produces `Failed extensions: 0` on a clean run, which is verbatim what B-2 requirement 4 forbids ('not a heading with nothing under it, not "0 failed"'), and BOTH of that case's assertions still pass, so bats reports `ok`. The check cannot fail on its own clause's failing example. Note this is a defect in the plan, not in the artifact: the four scripts are in fact clean (every `${arr[@]}` expansion at vscode:38-40, raycast:52-54 and claude-plugins:95-97 is guarded by a `[ "${#arr[@]}" -gt 0 ]` count test, and no clean run prints a summary), so the check would return PASS either way. That is the problem. A check that returns the right answer regardless of the artifact is not falsifiable, and B-2 and B-5 are both blocker clauses whose last remaining carrier this is. Fix: replace 'read the output of the four cases' with the reconstruction spelled out, citing where the fixtures live so the checker can copy them exactly (tests/install-failures.bats:31-35 render_script, :49-65 stub_defaults/stub_sleep, and the per-case success stubs at :118-127, :181, :250-251, :335-344), and add one sentence stating that a TAP `ok` line is not evidence for this clause.
findings.evidence: T-005.md:30-35 (the check_method bullet). Demonstration 1, output route: `bats --show-output-of-passing-tests --filter 'all items succeed' tests/install-failures.bats` -> `1..4 / ok 1 install-packages: all items succeed... / ok 2 install-vscode-extensions... / ok 3 configure-raycast... / ok 4 install-claude-plugins...` and nothing else. Demonstration 2, undetectable defect: mutated copy of run_onchange_install-vscode-extensions.sh.tmpl with `echo "Failed extensions: ${#failed[@]}"` added after the success line, rendered and run with a success `code` stub, emits `Installing VS Code extensions...` / `VS Code extensions installed.` / `Failed extensions: 0`; the case's assertions at tests/install-failures.bats:185-186 evaluate to assert_contains 'VS Code extensions installed.' -> PASS and assert_not_contains 'could not install' -> PASS. Artifact-is-clean evidence: grep -nE 'set -[eu]|\[@\]|declare -A' over the four scripts returns only guarded expansions.

findings.description: D-4's boltdb check anchors to a reference point that drifts forward past the work it polices. Both the constitution and T-006 phrase it as 'chezmoistate.boltdb mtime no later than the job's first task file', but task files are rewritten every time the orchestrator moves a status, so that reference moves. Measured: T-001.md was born 2026-08-06 22:44:02 and its mtime now reads 2026-08-07 13:52:40, fifteen hours later. The check as written therefore tolerates any `chezmoi apply` between job start and 13:52 today, a window that covers the whole of T-001's and T-004's execution (their verdicts landed 2026-08-06 23:29-23:30). It does not change the outcome here, because boltdb's mtime is 2026-08-06 20:26:14, earlier than the spec file itself, so no apply happened and the check will genuinely pass. Fix: anchor to something nobody rewrites - `.agent-guild/state/spec.md` (mtime 2026-08-06 20:34:28) or the literal 2026-08-06 20:50 CDT the constitution's own operational precondition records.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:270, T-006.md:24-25. `stat -f '%SB birth %Sm mod'`: T-001.md birth 2026-08-06 22:44:02, mod 2026-08-07 13:52:40; spec.md birth/mod 2026-08-06 20:34:27/28; chezmoistate.boltdb mod 2026-08-06 20:26:14. Verdict timestamps T-001-haiku-r0.json 2026-08-06 23:30, T-004-haiku-r0.json 2026-08-06 23:29.

findings.description: Four deterministic checks now sit on checker-judgment tasks, which deviates from the routing table's 'a clause checked by a script routes to checker-deterministic'. This is the safe direction of the deviation - opus can run a git command, haiku cannot apply a rubric - and both check_methods write down a real reason for it, since a task has exactly one checker and these checks are timing-bound: D-1's script reads only the working tree and goes vacuous once T-006 commits, and V-2's 'green with the new coverage in place' is only true on the last task before that commit. Accepting it, but it should be recorded as deliberate rather than left to look like drift, because a future reader comparing tasks against the routing table will otherwise read it as the r2 defect repeating in mirror image.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md routing table, haiku row ('all deterministic checks (they only run scripts)') and the 'Route a task by the work' paragraph. T-005.md:8 `checker: checker-judgment` with :10-29 carrying D-1 and V-2; T-006.md:8 with :21-25 carrying D-4's repo-state half.

findings.description: T-005's routing note is correct about the diagnosis and has no lifecycle transition behind it. It says a FAIL on V-2, D-1, B-2 or B-5 must name T-001/T-002/T-003 as the owner so rework does not land on a prose worker. All three are `complete`, and the status table has no transition out of `complete` - the retry ladder only re-dispatches the same task's executor. T-006 depends on T-005, so a FAIL routed that way parks the job with no defined next move and the Stop gate holding the turn open. The note should say what the orchestrator actually does: reopen the owning task by setting it back to `assigned`, increment its retries, and leave T-005 at `checking` pending the re-check.
findings.evidence: T-005.md:36-39 (routing note). T-002.md:27 `status: complete`, T-003.md:29 `status: complete`, T-001.md:14 `status: complete`. T-006.md:29 `deps: [T-001, T-002, T-003, T-004, T-005]`. CLAUDE.md task lifecycle table, which lists `complete` as terminal.

findings.description: Confirming your count independently, and you have it right. V-1's table yields 10 pass and 5 fail at 1dec91c, not 7 and 8. Arithmetic from the table alone, without reference to any run: passing are the three `absent tool skips clean` cases for install-packages, install-vscode-extensions and install-claude-plugins (3), all three `one failure does not stop the rest` regression guards (3), and all four `all items succeed prints no failure summary` cases (4), totalling 10. Failing are `configure-raycast: absent tool skips clean` (1) and all four `present tool failing names the item` (4), totalling 5. The file carries exactly 15 `@test` blocks and their titles map one-to-one onto the table's rows, so no row is double-counted or missing. The checker of record's '7 pass, 8 fail, exactly as the constitution specified' is wrong on both numbers; the total is right, which is what let it pass unremarked. T-003 standing `complete` is correct on the merits.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:159-167 (V-1's per-case table). `grep -n '^@test' tests/install-failures.bats` returns 15 titles at :90, :97, :116, :137, :144, :161, :179, :194, :202, :225, :246, :268, :275, :304, :333, matching the table's rows exactly. T-003.md:132-147 records the same 10/5 split from your re-run.

findings.description: V-2 fires at T-005 and will pass. Re-derived rather than taken on report. `timeout 400 bats tests/` exits 0 in 36 seconds over 117 cases, so the check_method's 300-second timeout has a 8x margin and the new file's fifteen template renders do not threaten it. Every per-file @test floor holds: apps 18/18, doctor 11/10, font 44/44, jsonc 9/9, licensed-fonts 7/7, packages 13/13. The replacement skip grep is sound and is an improvement on the diff form it replaces: `grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*skip\b' tests/*.bats` returns nothing across all seven files including the untracked install-failures.bats, `skip\b` does not match the mandated `skips clean` titles because `skip` followed by `s` is not a word boundary, and there is no pre-existing `skip` anywhere in the suite for the stricter form to trip over.
findings.evidence: `time (timeout 400 bats tests/)` -> exit 0, 36.227s total, last line `ok 117 every bundle in the catalog is reachable from some role's defaults`. `grep -c '^@test'` per file: apps 18, doctor 11, font 44, jsonc 9, licensed-fonts 7, packages 13, install-failures 15. `grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*skip\b' tests/*.bats` -> no output, exit 1.

findings.description: D-1 fires at T-005 and will pass, and the two ways it could have gone vacuous or falsely failed are both closed. The exact command in the check_method exits 0 with `OK: 9 path(s) in scope` against the tree as it stands. The script's path set is the union of `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` and `git diff --name-only`, so the untracked tests/install-failures.bats is seen and lands under the `tests/` prefix rather than being missed - `--untracked-files=all` is explicitly there to stop git collapsing a new directory into one entry. And `.agent-guild/state/` is carved out in `in_scope()` unconditionally, so the orchestrator's own task, verdict and log writes cannot trip the check, which was the false-FAIL risk given the job's bookkeeping sits inside the repo. Timing is right too: T-005 is the last task that leaves the tree dirty, and T-006 commits after.
findings.evidence: `python3 .agent-guild/scripts/check-diff-scope.py --ignore dot_claude/encrypted_private_settings.json.age <allowlist>` -> `OK: 9 path(s) in scope`, exit 0. check-diff-scope.py `collect_changed_paths()` and its `--untracked-files=all` docstring; `in_scope()` `if path.startswith('.agent-guild/state/'): return True`. `git status --porcelain -uall` lists 8 modified plus `?? tests/install-failures.bats`.

findings.description: D-4's load-bearing assumption holds, and it was worth checking because the job would have broken it if it did not. The suite renders templates fifteen times through `chezmoi execute-template`, and T-005's checker runs the whole suite again before T-006's boltdb check. If `execute-template` touched the persistent state database, the mtime check would fire falsely on work the job itself did. It does not: I ran the full suite today and chezmoistate.boltdb's mtime is still 2026-08-06 20:26:14, which predates even spec.md. The other three deterministic bullets are also clean - .chezmoidata.toml appears in neither `git status --porcelain` nor any diff, and `git rev-list 1dec91c..HEAD` is empty so the shared push check has nothing to contain yet.
findings.evidence: `stat -f '%Sm' ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoistate.boltdb` -> 2026-08-06 20:26:14, taken after `timeout 400 bats tests/` completed. tests/install-failures.bats:31-35 `render_script` calls `chezmoi execute-template` once per case. `git status --porcelain -uall` does not list .chezmoidata.toml. `git rev-list 1dec91c..HEAD` -> empty.

findings.description: B-5's static half is not orphaned, which was the thing to check given T-005 carries only a partial version of it. T-005's grep covers `${var^^}` and `declare -A` but drops the `[@]` unguarded-expansion judgment and the `set -e`/`set -u` greps the clause names. Those did fire, at T-002, whose check_method assigned the full static rubric to checker-judgment before the task went complete, and the four scripts have not changed since. Re-derived against the artifact: three of the four scripts set `-e`, none sets `-u`, there are no associative arrays and no `${var^^}`, and every array expansion is preceded by its count test. T-002's version did omit the `set -e`/`set -u` greps the clause lists, which is a check_method narrower than its clause, but the scripts are frozen and the property they were meant to establish holds, so there is nothing left to catch.
findings.evidence: T-002.md:20-22 (B-5 static rubric, checker-judgment) with T-002.md:27 `status: complete`; T-005.md:35 (the partial grep). `grep -nE 'set -[eu]|\[@\]|declare -A' over the four scripts: install-packages none; install-vscode-extensions :10 `set -e`, :38 `if [ "${#failed[@]}" -gt 0 ]`, :40 expansion; configure-raycast :10 `set -e`, :52 guard, :54 expansion; install-claude-plugins :21 `set -e`, :95 guard, :97 expansion.

findings.description: The two prose clauses fire where they should. D-2's rubric on T-005 is the clause text restated and its checker is the right family; _working-memory/conventions.md is already modified in the tree and decisionLog.md is not yet, which is consistent with a worker mid-flight and is exactly what the 'FAIL if decisionLog.md has no entry' bullet exists to catch if it stays that way. D-3 on T-006 carries all four of the clause's evidence sources including the `git branch -r --contains` push check that replaced the range form, and it runs after the commit, which is where the post-commit scope diff has to land given D-1's script cannot read a range. Nothing in this job re-runs the suite after T-006 commits, and nothing needs to: committing does not change file contents, and V-2 has already fired on T-005 against the same bytes.
findings.evidence: T-005.md:40-45 against constitution.md:243. T-006.md:10-15 against constitution.md:250-256. `git status --porcelain` shows ` M _working-memory/conventions.md` and no entry for _working-memory/decisionLog.md.
